method: N-1: remove each component, evaluate every flow. severity = flow weight x impact x recovery penalty

bgp_silent_s.source: measured 2026-11-23 (Test 3, reset of Azure gateway instance0 = 2 of 4 tunnels): 6 of 16 ECMP flows (38 %) had a 22-31 s gap while the BGP hold timer expired; the other 10 never dropped a packet. Replaces the earlier 90 s estimate (upper end of the plan's 30-90 s).
bgp_silent_s.measured_impact: 6 of 16 flows (38 %) for 2 of 4 tunnels lost; the model uses the tunnel share (50 %), ECMP hashing of 16 flows gave 38 %

bgp_clean_withdrawal_s.source: measured 2026-11-23 (Test 3, wrong peer ASN on one tunnel with IPsec up, held 3.5 min): the peer rejected the BGP OPEN with a NOTIFICATION, the routes were withdrawn and ECMP moved the flows; 0 of 16 flows lost a packet at 5 pings/s. v1 B1: 0.8 s gap on an admin BGP reset.

azure_gw_instance_rebuild_s.source: measured 2026-11-23 (Test 3): after the instance0 reset, traffic had recovered in ~30 s, but all 4 tunnels were UP with routes again only after 14 min 20 s. The link ran on 2 of 4 tunnels until then.

tgw_route_convergence_s.source: measured 2026-11-23 (Test 4 break A / restore A): TGW route-table changes are not atomic. After the propagation was removed, 14-20 % of requests still got through in the first seconds; after it was restored, 87-95 % got through in the first seconds, then 100 %. 'A few seconds' each way.

appliance_mode_transition_s.source: measured 2026-11-23 (Test 4 restore B): re-enabling appliance mode on live traffic re-pinned the TGW's AZ hashing; 22-40 % of new flows succeeded for several minutes (fw-invalid drops 50 -> 404 on fw-a, 39 -> 364 on fw-b) and it was back to 100 % within ~14 min, without intervention.

dns_failover_s.source: measured 2026-11-23 (Tests 1-2): app loss with Route 53 unreachable failed over in 36.4 s (Test 1, Traffic Manager 10 s probes, TTL 30); app + VPN loss in 41.7 s user-visible (Test 2; Route 53 answered Azure at +40.6 s, Traffic Manager at +35.4 s). v1 (Route 53 only, 60 s alias TTL) measured 77-128.5 s.

dns_provider_retry_s.source: measured 2026-11-23 (Test 1 provider loss): with every Route 53 name server dropped, unbound answered 20/20 from Azure DNS with median +142 ms (cold) / +124 ms (warm infra cache). Adaptive retransmit (~376 ms) and fast server switching, not a full 3 s timeout. Other resolvers may differ.

dnsmasq_retry_s.source: Estimate: dnsmasq marks an upstream dead after a timeout and uses the other listed server.

eks_node_loss_s.source: v1 Test 3 tuned average 56.8 s of user-visible failures after losing one EKS node (docs/archive/v1/results.md).

rows.name: TGW appliance mode on the inspection attachment

transition_risk.summary: Changing appliance_mode_support on live traffic, in either direction, re-pins the TGW's AZ hashing: measured up to ~14 min of asymmetric drops (22-40 % of new flows succeeded) when it was re-enabled. Set it at build time; change it only in a maintenance window.
transition_risk.source: measured 2026-11-23 (Test 4 restore B): re-enabling appliance mode on live traffic re-pinned the TGW's AZ hashing; 22-40 % of new flows succeeded for several minutes (fw-invalid drops 50 -> 404 on fw-a, 39 -> 364 on fw-b) and it was back to 100 % within ~14 min, without intervention.

fixes.mitigation: Run mindbridge precheck on every plan, and a Reachability Analyzer path check after apply
